# enori_monitor (Resource)

Manages an Enori uptime monitor.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A website monitor with keyword + status-code checks and alerting.
resource "enori_monitor" "marketing_site" {
  name                 = "Marketing site"
  url                  = "https://www.example.com"
  type                 = "website"
  interval_seconds     = 60
  expected_status_code = 200
  expected_keyword     = "Welcome"
  follow_redirects     = true
  alert_on_down        = true
  alert_on_recovered   = true
  tags                 = ["production", "marketing"]
}

# A grouped API health check that notifies specific alert channels.
resource "enori_monitor" "api_health" {
  name                 = "Public API health"
  group_name           = "Production"
  url                  = "https://api.example.com/health"
  type                 = "website"
  interval_seconds     = 30
  expected_status_code = 200
  failure_threshold    = 2
  alert_channel_ids    = ["chan_abc123", "chan_def456"]
}

# A raw TCP port check.
resource "enori_monitor" "db_port" {
  name             = "Postgres port"
  url              = "db.example.com"
  type             = "port"
  port             = 5432
  interval_seconds = 60
}

# A DNS monitor.
resource "enori_monitor" "primary_dns" {
  name             = "Primary DNS"
  url              = "example.com"
  type             = "dns"
  interval_seconds = 300
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Human-readable monitor name (1–100 chars).
- `type` (String) Monitor type (lowercase): `website`, `ping`, `port`, `dns`, `domain`, or `job`. Changing the type forces a new monitor (the type is immutable).
- `url` (String) Target URL or host to monitor.

### Optional

- `alert_channel_ids` (Set of String) IDs of alert channels to notify.
- `alert_on_down` (Boolean) Send an alert when the monitor goes down. Server default: true.
- `alert_on_recovered` (Boolean) Send an alert when the monitor recovers. Server default: true.
- `custom_user_agent` (String) Custom User-Agent header for website checks (max 512 chars).
- `expected_keyword` (String) Keyword that must appear in the response body (website checks).
- `expected_status_code` (Number) Expected HTTP status code (100–599) for website checks. Server default: 200.
- `failure_threshold` (Number) Consecutive failures before the monitor is marked down (0–10).
- `follow_redirects` (Boolean) Whether to follow HTTP redirects (website checks). Server default: true.
- `group_name` (String) Optional group the monitor belongs to.
- `http_method` (String) HTTP method for website checks (e.g. `GET`, `POST`, `HEAD`). Server default: `GET`.
- `interval_seconds` (Number) Check interval in seconds (30–31104000). Server default: 300.
- `port` (Number) Target port (1–65535) for port checks.
- `request_body` (String) Request body sent with the check (e.g. for POST website checks).
- `ssl_expiry_warning_days` (Number) Days before SSL expiry to warn (7, 14, 30, or 60). Server default: 30.
- `tags` (Set of String) Tags for organizing and filtering monitors (lowercase alphanumeric + hyphens).
- `timeout_seconds` (Number) Per-check timeout in seconds (5–300). Server default: 30.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Monitor identifier assigned by Enori.
